literal: Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun
idiomatic: Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun

literal: Man's nature and spirit, what he receives at birth, may differ; rigidity and softness are distinct, urgency and ease take shape against each other—few deeply examine right and wrong, and none fail to give full play to feeling and desire.
idiomatic: Human nature differs at birth; rigidity and softness, urgency and ease shape one another—few truly weigh right and wrong, and nearly all indulge feeling and desire.

literal: As for those who closely observe fire and water and again wear the girdle-weights of caution, they are rare.
idiomatic: Those who watch fire and water closely and wear the girdle of restraint are rare indeed.

literal: Prison clerks as a scourge—their origin is of long standing.
idiomatic: Prison clerks as a scourge—their origin is ancient.

literal: From the time Wei lost the contest for the realm, the net leaked across the world; Gao Huan punished its lax slackness and also used stern majesty to master things, so that inner and outer officials all knew the prohibitory mesh.
idiomatic: When Wei lost hold of the realm the law's net gaped wide; Gao Huan punished lax rule and governed with stern majesty until every official, within and without, knew the prohibitory mesh.

literal: Now Di Zhen and the rest are recorded to preserve Cruel Officials, as warning and encouragement.
idiomatic: Here Di Zhen and the rest are recorded under Cruel Officials, as warning and encouragement.

literal: Di Zhen, style Bao'an, was originally a man of Shangquyang in Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Di Zhen, style Bao'an, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan.

literal: He followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army and was appointed chief clerk.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army and was made chief clerk.

literal: His nature was stern and violent; in seeking and taking he knew no satiety.
idiomatic: Stern and violent by nature, he sought and took without satiety.

literal: Later he also held concurrent posts as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with the Traveling Court, directing all military affairs.
idiomatic: He later also served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner of the Traveling Court, directing military affairs.

literal: Zhen ruled subordinates with cruel severity; the host of officers lost heart, and the people killed him.
idiomatic: Zhen ruled subordinates with cruel severity; his officers lost heart and the people killed him.

literal: Later he was posthumously given Ding province.
idiomatic: He was later posthumously made inspector of Ding province.

literal: Song Youdao was a man of Guangping; his ancestors had moved there from Dunhuang.
idiomatic: Song Youdao was from Guangping; his ancestors had moved there from Dunhuang.

literal: His father Jiyu was prefect of Bohai.
idiomatic: His father Jiyu was prefect of Bohai.

literal: In his weak-capping years Youdao followed his father in the commandery; when his father died, gifts from clerks and people he accepted not one.
idiomatic: As a youth Youdao followed his father in the commandery; when his father died he accepted no gift from clerks or people.

literal: He served his mother and was known for filial piety.
idiomatic: He served his mother and was known for filial piety.

literal: He lived apart from his uncle; the uncle had a slave falsely accuse him of treason—Youdao lured the slave to return, cleared the charge, and killed him.
idiomatic: Living apart from an uncle whose slave falsely accused him of treason, Youdao lured the slave back, cleared the charge, and killed him.

literal: When Wei Prince of Guangyang campaigned north, Youdao was requested as armor-cases staff; when he became inspector of Ding province, Youdao was again made staff officer of his office.
idiomatic: When the Wei Prince of Guangyang marched north, Youdao was requested as armor-cases staff; as inspector of Ding he again made Youdao a staff officer.

literal: The Prince of Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong; Yuan Hui slandered him as having surrendered to the bandits and seized his wife and children—Youdao pleaded and won their release, and with the prince's son escorted the coffin back for burial.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong; Yuan Hui slandered him for surrendering to bandits and seized his family—Youdao pleaded and freed them and with the prince's son escorted the coffin home for burial.

literal: Commandant Li Shanchang admired his integrity and spirit and brought him in as palace attendant censor; within the Terrace they said: "To see a bandit and be able to attack him—that is Song Youdao."
idiomatic: Commandant Li Shanchang admired his spirit and made him palace attendant censor; within the Terrace they said: "See a bandit and strike— that is Song Youdao."

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Youdao was made Left Central Army Bureau gentleman; censured by Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Huaiyang Yuan Ye, Youdao held his board and made a long bow, saying: "Your servant thanks the prince's anger, not the prince's reason."
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Youdao became Left Central Army Bureau gentleman; censured by Director Yuan Ye of Huaiyang, Youdao held his board and bowed: "I thank your anger, my lord, not your reasoning."

literal: That same day he went to the palace and submitted a memorial: "Xuzhou inspector Yuan Fu has repeatedly memorialized that 'the false Liang is broadly raising troops to take Pengcheng; I beg an added two thousand guardsmen.'
idiomatic: That day he memorialized the throne: "Xuzhou inspector Yuan Fu has repeatedly written that 'false Liang is raising troops against Pengcheng; I beg two thousand more guardsmen.'"

literal: Fu is a weighty minister of the imperial clan; his plea should be real, so I measured and memorialized to grant a thousand military officers.
idiomatic: Fu is a weighty clansman; his plea should be genuine, so I measured and memorialized a grant of a thousand military officers.

literal: Fu now leaves his post; citing blocked roads he keeps them for self-defense, yet takes in the eight hundred guardsmen left on defense, pleading that 'the borders are quiet and I beg to send them home.'
idiomatic: Fu now leaves his post; citing blocked roads he keeps the men for self-defense, yet takes in eight hundred guardsmen on defense, pleading the borders are quiet and begging to send them home.

literal: Your servant is charged with this bureau and knows deeply this cannot be.
idiomatic: I serve this bureau and know this cannot stand.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Huaiyang Yuan Ye is Fu's brother's son; within three days his clerk Xie Yuan pressed eight times that it should be allowed by precedent.
idiomatic: Director Yuan Ye of Huaiyang is Fu's nephew; within three days his clerk Xie Yuan pressed eight times for approval by precedent.

literal: Your servant dared not attach below and deceive above, betraying the sage clarity.
idiomatic: I dared not attach below and deceive above, betraying Your Majesty's clarity.

literal: Yet Fu, while in office, begged troops in succession; when he left his post he at once asked release—advancing and retreating for himself, with no thought for the state.
idiomatic: Yet Fu, in office, begged troops in succession; once replaced he at once asked release—acting for himself, not for the state.

literal: The request does not fit; his crime is of the lower grade.
idiomatic: The request does not fit; his crime is of the lower grade.

literal: Or they even summoned your servant to the Masters of Writing main hall and said: 'You, a petty gentleman—can care for the state in your heart be thicker than mine?'
idiomatic: Or they summoned me to the Masters of Writing hall: 'You petty gentleman—is your care for the state thicker than mine?'

literal: Ugly abuse overflowed their mouths, heedless of court regulations; Right Vice Director Chen Shilong, Bureau gentleman Xue Ju, and more than a hundred below all heard and saw.
idiomatic: Ugly abuse overflowed their mouths, heedless of court law; Vice Director Chen Shilong, Bureau gentleman Xue Ju, and more than a hundred others heard and saw.

literal: Your servant truly offered straight words: 'Loyal ministers serve the state—the matter is in the heart; what does it matter whether one is base or noble?
idiomatic: I offered straight words: 'Loyal ministers serve the state in the heart—what matter base or noble?'

literal: Since you entered Luoyang from Beihai you could not die in the difficulty, yet cleared the palace to welcome violent rebels.
idiomatic: Since you entered Luoyang from Beihai you could not die in the crisis, yet cleared the palace to welcome violent rebels.

literal: Zheng Xianhu raised righteousness in Guangzhou and you again raised banners to attack him.
idiomatic: Zheng Xianhu raised righteousness in Guangzhou and you again raised banners to attack him.

literal: You rush to evil like a stream, yet fell the good—how swift!
idiomatic: You rush to evil like a stream and fell the good—how swift!

literal: Now crowned above the hundred officials, you yet wish to harm the government for private ends.'
idiomatic: Now crowned above the hundred officials, you wish to harm government for private ends.'

literal: For these words of your servant, Ye's gift of anger grew still worse.
idiomatic: For these words Ye's anger grew worse.

literal: Your servant is unworthy and has offended a noble minister; I beg to be relieved of the bureau gentleman post."
idiomatic: Unworthy, I have offended a noble minister; I beg relief from bureau gentleman."

literal: The emperor summoned and received Youdao, praising and comforting him.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned Youdao, praised and comforted him.

literal: Ye also memorialized: "Your servant crowns the hundred officials, yet a single gentleman rolls up his sleeves and speaks loudly, freely speaking to blunt and humiliate; I beg to be relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing."
idiomatic: Ye also memorialized: "I crown the hundred officials, yet one gentleman rolls up his sleeves and speaks loudly to blunt me; I beg relief from Director of the Masters of Writing."

literal: The emperor then issued an edict allowing relief of the Terrace gentleman.
idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict allowing relief of the Terrace gentleman.

literal: Later he was made Central Army staff officer of Si province.
idiomatic: He was later made Central Army staff officer of Si province.

literal: When about to return to Ye, continuous rain piled travelers at the Yellow River bridge.
idiomatic: When about to return to Ye, rain piled travelers at the Yellow River bridge.

literal: Youdao morning and evening feasted and sang under the awning; travelers said: "What season is this to make such sounds—you are truly a great fool."
idiomatic: Youdao feasted and sang under the awning morning and evening; travelers said: "What season is this for such song—you are a great fool."

literal: Youdao answered: "What season is there when one should not make such sounds—you too are a great fool."
idiomatic: Youdao answered: "What season when one should not sing? You too are a great fool."

literal: Also a great fool."
idiomatic: Also a great fool."

literal: Later Gao Huan came from Taiyuan to court and on seeing him said: "Is this man Song Youdao?
idiomatic: When Gao Huan came from Taiyuan to court he said: "Is this Song Youdao?

literal: I have often heard the name; today I first know his face."
idiomatic: I have often heard the name; today I first see his face."

literal: Youdao was transferred to vice governor.
idiomatic: Youdao was transferred to vice governor.

literal: Some days later, when Gao Huan was in Si province feasting court gentlemen, he raised his cup and turned to Youdao: "He who drinks wine from Gao Huan's hand is a great man; your person fits drinking this wine.
idiomatic: Days later at Si province Gao Huan feasted court gentlemen, raised his cup to Youdao: "He who drinks Gao Huan's wine is a great man; you fit this cup.

literal: " On returning to Jinyang, the hundred officials took leave at Ziyang.
idiomatic: " Returning to Jinyang, officials took leave at Ziyang.

literal: Gao Huan took Youdao's hand and said: "I know well that among court nobles some hate and envy you; only use your heart, do not harbor fear—I shall make your rank resemble theirs."
idiomatic: Gao Huan took his hand: "I know nobles hate you; use your heart, fear nothing—I shall make your rank like theirs."

literal: Thereupon he memorialized to make Youdao commandant.
idiomatic: He memorialized to make Youdao commandant.

literal: Gao Cheng pressed the request; thus Cui Xian was made censor-in-chief and Youdao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng pressed the request; Cui Xian became censor-in-chief and Youdao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Gao Cheng told Xian and Youdao: "One of you holds the Southern Terrace, one the Northern Bureau—you should make the realm stand in awe."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng told them: "One holds the Southern Terrace, one the Northern Bureau—make the realm stand in awe."

literal: Youdao entered the province and impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister Hou Jing, Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Bi, Director Sima Ziru and others for official loans of gold and silver, pressing for repayment; though not pointed bribery, in the end he did not avoid the powerful.
idiomatic: Entering office, Youdao impeached Grand Tutor Wang Tan of Xianyang, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister Hou Jing, Director Yuan Bi, Director Sima Ziru and others for official loans of gold and silver—though not direct bribery, he did not spare the powerful.

literal: He also memorialized and rejected several hundred failures of the Masters of Writing; powerful clerks Wang Ru and the rest were all flogged and driven off.
idiomatic: He memorialized hundreds of Masters of Writing failures; powerful clerks Wang Ru and others were flogged and driven off.

literal: At first according to precedent, at the Masters of Writing reception a gate name was set to record coming and going morning and evening; from servants downward all looked askance.
idiomatic: By precedent a gate register recorded comings and goings at the Masters of Writing; from servants down all looked askance.

literal: When Prince of Anping Wang sat in a matter and perished, Zhangwu's two princes and the various princes' consorts and grand consorts who were his close kin were all summoned to account.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Anping perished, Zhangwu's two princes and related consorts and grand consorts were all summoned to account.

literal: Bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun directed the matter; where there was a memorial he forbade, where there was none he still forbade.
idiomatic: Bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun directed the matter—memorial or no, he forbade.

literal: Youdao judged and sent down to the Court of Justice for punishment; Gao Longzhi disagreed; thereupon in reverse he slandered Youdao for stern color and insulting himself, and falsely examined group clerks to prove it, and with Vice Director Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu, Director Zheng Suzu and others memorialized:
idiomatic: Youdao sent the case to the Court of Justice; Gao Longzhi disagreed and slandered Youdao for stern insults, falsely examining clerks to prove it; with Vice Director Wang Xu of Xiangcheng, Director Zheng Suzu and others he memorialized:

literal: Adorning falsehood and confusing truth—what state law must remove;
idiomatic: Adorning falsehood and confusing truth—state law must remove it;

literal: attaching below and deceiving above—what royal government cannot bear.
idiomatic: attaching below and deceiving above—royal government cannot bear it.

literal: We respectfully find Left Vice Director Song Youdao—his fame and standing originally deficient, his merit and record—what tally?
idiomatic: We find Left Vice Director Song Youdao—fame deficient, merit unrecorded:

literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, court gentlemen scattered in flight; in a time of dearth of men he stole the Terrace gentleman post.
idiomatic: at Yong'an's start, when court gentlemen fled, he stole a Terrace post in dearth of men.

literal: Restless conduct and fawning words, giving full play to his treachery; he rarely knew righteousness, heedless of canonical text; men despised his heart, the crowd feared his mouth.
idiomatic: Restless and fawning, full of treachery; heedless of canon; men despised him, crowds feared his mouth.

literal: Going out to provinces, entering the Secretariat, he repeatedly held pure posts, yet long did evil without repentance, never restrained; praise and blame were his own, hatred and favor at his whim.
idiomatic: Out to provinces, in the Secretariat on pure posts, he long did evil unrepentant; praise and blame were his, hatred his whim.

literal: Recently because of the Prince of Anping Wang matter he then gave full play to his narrow heart, using public business to repay a grudge, mutually impeaching with bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun.
idiomatic: Recently over the Prince of Anping he gave play to narrow heart, repaying grudges through office, mutually impeaching with Bi Yiyun.

literal: Also Left Outer Army Bureau gentleman Wei Shudao's document said: 'Within the bureau surrendered men Zuo Ze and others were sent to the capital by the capital region with orders to release on guaranty.'
idiomatic: Also Wei Shudao of Left Outer Army Bureau wrote: 'Surrendered men Zuo Ze were sent to the capital with orders to release on guaranty.'

literal: When the great general was in the province he judged 'hear and allow.'
idiomatic: When the great general was in the province he judged 'allow.'

literal: Youdao grew angry and said: 'In past days what sort of office was that office, that you take this as precedent!'
idiomatic: Youdao raged: 'What sort of office was that, to take as precedent!'

literal: Also he said: 'Riding on a former edict pattern—what sort of edict pattern is that!'
idiomatic: Also: 'Riding a former edict—what edict is that!'

literal: Asked according to the matter, Youdao acknowledged all.
idiomatic: Questioned on the matter, Youdao acknowledged all.

literal: According to the code: 'Resisting and defying an edict-bearing envoy—without a minister's rites, great irreverence is death.'
idiomatic: By code: 'Resisting an edict-bearing envoy without minister's rites—death for great irreverence.'

literal: Resisting an envoy still earns death; how much more Youdao's unministered words, the crime of slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harboring robbers, deceiving the public and selling the law, receiving wrapped bribes—property following office thick, wealth with rank piled; though bribery was not yet exposed, treachery was such.
idiomatic: Resisting an envoy earns death; how much more unministered words, slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harbors robbers, deceiving the public, taking bribes—wealth piled with rank though bribery was not yet exposed.

literal: Citing this one corner, the rest of the fraud can be verified.
idiomatic: This one corner proves the rest.

literal: Now according to ritual and law we place Youdao in the death crime."
idiomatic: Now by ritual and law we place Youdao in the death crime."

literal: At the time court gentlemen all took sides, thinking Youdao would not succeed.
idiomatic: Court gentlemen took sides, thinking Youdao would fail.

literal: Yet Gao Cheng, hearing his words contending with Longzhi, told Yang Zunyan: "This is truly a straight, great, hard evil man."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng, hearing his clash with Longzhi, told Yang Zunyan: "This is truly a straight, hard, evil man."

literal: Zunyan said: "It is like keeping a dog—you take it for its barking; now if you kill it for barking too much, I fear later there will be no dog to bark."
idiomatic: Zunyan said: "Like a dog kept for barking—kill it for barking too much and later none will bark."

literal: An edict sent him to the Court of Justice; Youdao was sentenced to removal from name.
idiomatic: An edict sent him to the Court of Justice; Youdao was removed from office.

literal: Gao Cheng sent Yuan Jingkang to tell him: "You early follow me to Bing province, or else others in strategy will kill you."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Yuan Jingkang: "Follow me early to Bing—or others in strategy will kill you."

literal: Youdao followed to Jinyang and was made Traveling Court personnel director; also made advisory staff of Taiyuan Duke's opening office.
idiomatic: Youdao followed to Jinyang as Traveling Court personnel director and advisory staff of the Taiyuan Duke's office.

literal: When Prince of Pingyang was commandant, Youdao as advisory staff held the writing attendant censor post.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Pingyang was commandant, Youdao as advisory staff held writing attendant censor.

literal: Soon with his original post he concurrently held Secretariat Left chief administrator.
idiomatic: Soon he concurrently held Secretariat Left chief administrator.

literal: When Gao Cheng suspected Yellow Gate gentleman Wen Zisheng of knowing Yuan Jin's plot, he bound him in prison and starved him—he ate his ragged coat and died.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng suspected Wen Zisheng of Yuan Jin's plot, he bound and starved him—he ate his ragged coat and died.

literal: The corpse was cast by the roadside; Youdao collected and buried it.
idiomatic: The corpse was cast by the road; Youdao collected and buried it.

literal: Gao Cheng said: "I recently wrote to the nobles of the capital discussing court gentlemen—you are partial to factions; that will be one sickness.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said: "I wrote the capital nobles on court gentlemen—you lean to factions; that is one sickness.

literal: Now you are truly a man who weighs old ties and righteousness; that feeling cannot be taken away.
idiomatic: Now you truly weigh old ties and righteousness; that cannot be taken.

literal: I originally would not kill Zisheng—what do you fear in burying him?
idiomatic: I would not have killed Zisheng—what fear in burying him?

literal: Those in the world who would replace you in fear do not know my heart."
idiomatic: Those who would replace you in fear do not know my heart."

literal: Soon he was made censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: Soon he was made censor-in-chief.

literal: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi joined censor selection; beyond the limit he submitted a petition; Dao Xi was old friends with Youdao and had the clerk receive it.
idiomatic: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi joined censor selection and submitted beyond the limit; old friends with Youdao, he had the clerk receive it.

literal: Gao Cheng was angry, flogged Youdao and judged: "Youdao's nature is fierce and tough; right and wrong pour from his mouth; he blows hairs to wash away dirt and scars men's persons.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng flogged Youdao and judged: "Youdao is fierce; right and wrong pour from his mouth; he blows hairs to find dirt and scars men.

literal: Formerly he quarreled with bureau gentleman Lan Jingyun, listing ten items.
idiomatic: Formerly he quarreled with Lan Jingyun, listing ten items.

literal: When pushed and examined, they were empty and false.
idiomatic: Pushed and examined, they were false.

literal: Now together with Dao Xi he insults and violates the court canon—a judge who violates it is especially hard to forgive; he should be handed to the province for punishment."
idiomatic: Now with Dao Xi he insults court canon—a judge who violates it is hard to forgive; hand to the province."

literal: Youdao was imprisoned; prison clerks wished to remove his cangue; Youdao would not: "This is where orders are written—it cannot be lightly removed."
idiomatic: Imprisoned, clerks wished to remove his cangue; Youdao refused: "Orders are written here—it cannot be removed."

literal: Gao Cheng heard and pardoned him.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng heard and pardoned him.

literal: Youdao's upright will did not change.
idiomatic: Youdao's upright will did not change.
